concerns.concern: The singlet-triplet attribution in the title is not tested. A momentum-anisotropic or multiband s-wave gap (as in NbSe2, or one arising from the CDW-reconstructed Fermi surface) gives the same two-feature DOS. The supplement dismisses this alternative by assertion rather than calculation.
concerns.quote: The title claim is not tested... A momentum-anisotropic or multiband s-wave gap gives the same DOS.

concerns.concern: If SnS is superconducting, the exposed 1H layer sits on a second superconductor. A McMillan-type proximity bilayer would generically produce two gap features with no singlet-triplet physics. The 1H/SnS coupling must enter the analysis, and 'decoupled' must be reconciled with 'each gap unaffected by the other'.
concerns.quote: Proximity from the SnS layer is an alternative explanation for the second gap on the 1H termination.

concerns.concern: The model's mechanism relies on inverted 2H stacking that restores inversion. In the misfit compound the 1H layers have the same orientation, so mixing stays symmetry-allowed at any t_perp. The bilayer model therefore does not describe this compound or support the link to decoupling.
concerns.quote: In that stacking, interlayer coupling does not restore inversion, and singlet-triplet mixing stays symmetry-allowed at any t_perp.

concerns.concern: The arguments for intrinsic superconductivity in SnS (same critical field, vortices, same coherence length, gap size) are what proximity of an atomically thin layer would also predict. They therefore do not exclude an induced gap.
concerns.quote: Most of the listed observations are therefore what proximity predicts, not evidence against it.

concerns.concern: The two-gap fit is compared only with an isotropic single-gap fit. A single anisotropic gap (gap distribution or angular form) should be tried as a third alternative; if it fits equally well, the claim should be 'an anisotropic gap'.
concerns.quote: A fit with an anisotropic single gap... as a third alternative. If that fits as well, "two gaps" should be "an anisotropic gap".

concerns.concern: The two-band dirty-limit Hc2 fits return different coupling constants for the two field orientations, although the coupling matrix is a material property. A joint fit with shared lambda_ij is needed.
concerns.quote: the BCS coupling matrix is a property of the material and must be shared by both fits. A joint fit with common lambda_ij is needed.

concerns.concern: A control calculation is requested with spin-orbit coupling set to zero at t_perp = 0. This removes inversion breaking and the triplet channel, and would show whether the two-gap feature then disappears.
concerns.quote: lambda -> 0 at t_perp = 0. This removes inversion breaking, and with it the triplet channel, inside the same model.

concerns.concern: A control calculation is requested in which the t_perp sweep is repeated with the triplet channel switched off. This would show that a purely A1g anisotropic gap does not respond to t_perp in the same way.
concerns.quote: The same t_perp sweep with the triplet channel switched off by hand

concerns.concern: At least one experiment that separates the singlet-triplet scenario from conventional alternatives is needed. Suggestions are the in-plane-field dependence of both gap features, their temperature dependence, and the sensitivity of the smaller gap to nonmagnetic disorder.
concerns.quote: the authors should identify and attempt at least one measurement that separates the two scenarios.

concerns.concern: Unless a discriminating test is added, the title and abstract should be reworded to say the data are consistent with, and motivate, a singlet-triplet scenario rather than demonstrate it.
concerns.quote: the title and abstract should be reworded to say that the data are consistent with, and motivate, a singlet-triplet scenario

concerns.concern: The temperature dependence of Delta1 and Delta2 from STS should be measured. This is the standard and cheap test for two-band superconductivity.
concerns.quote: The temperature dependence of Delta1 and Delta2 from STS. This is the standard test for two-band superconductivity

concerns.concern: Field-dependent spectra exist but the small-gap feature is not analyzed. In two-band systems it is typically suppressed much faster.
concerns.quote: S4 shows spectra at 0, 1, 2 and 3 kG, but the small-gap feature is not analyzed.

concerns.concern: The single-gap fit needs an effective temperature of 900 mK at a 270 mK base temperature. This signals a broadening mechanism other than thermal smearing.
concerns.quote: The single-gap fit needs an effective temperature of 900 mK at a base temperature of 270 mK

concerns.concern: All fit parameters for both models (T_eff, Dynes Gamma, weights N1, N2) should be reported with uncertainties and a goodness-of-fit measure. The two-gap model has more free parameters, so a better fit alone is expected.
concerns.quote: The two-gap model has two more free parameters, so a better fit alone is expected.

concerns.concern: The 300 ueV 'kink' is only a shoulder on the main d2I/dV2 peak and is marked only at positive bias. The authors should show it appears symmetrically at negative bias and is robust.
concerns.quote: The authors should show that the feature appears symmetrically at negative bias and that it is robust.

concerns.concern: Reproducibility of the two-gap spectrum across tips, cleaves and samples is not shown. The only spatial data are 150 spectra along one 45 nm line.
concerns.quote: Reproducibility across tips, cleaves and samples. S3 is 150 spectra along one 45 nm line.

concerns.concern: The lock-in modulation amplitude and the effective energy resolution for the low-energy spectra are not given.
concerns.quote: The methods give no Vmod for Fig. 4

concerns.concern: The lock-in frequency is inconsistent between the methods and the figure captions.
concerns.quote: the frequency is 907 Hz in the methods but 870 Hz in the Fig. 1 captions.

concerns.concern: The dirty-limit Hc2 model conflicts with the clean-enough limit needed for a strongly anisotropic s+f gap to survive. The mean free path should be estimated from rho0 and compared with xi.
concerns.quote: The authors should estimate the mean free path from rho0 and compare it with xi.

concerns.concern: For in-plane field in an Ising superconductor with anisotropy 19, Hc2 is set by spin physics and 2D geometry. An orbital Gurevich-type model is the wrong functional form, so the fit says little about two gaps.
concerns.quote: An orbital Gurevich-type model is the wrong functional form for that orientation, so the fit says little about two gaps.

concerns.concern: Upward curvature of Hc2(T) has other known origins, such as dimensional crossover or the SnS/TaS2 two-component structure. It need not reflect two gaps within 1H.
concerns.quote: the curvature could equally reflect the SnS/TaS2 two-component structure, not two gaps within 1H.

concerns.concern: The model must be connected to experiment quantitatively. The paper should give the realistic effective t_perp for bulk 2H-TaS2 at the relevant pockets and an ARPES upper bound on t_perp in the misfit. This would show which side of the ~0.24 eV crossover each falls on.
concerns.quote: Otherwise the model does not actually connect to the claimed experimental correlation.

concerns.concern: The interlayer hopping is taken as k-independent. In H-type TMDs it is strongly suppressed at K, where the model's two-gap feature lives, so a constant t_perp overstates the coupling.
concerns.quote: The hopping t_perp is k-independent. In H-type TMDs, interlayer hopping is strongly momentum-dependent

concerns.concern: The model omits the CDW, whose wavevector (0.3543 Q_Bragg) differs from 2H-TaS2. Because the CDW reconstructs the K-pocket Fermi surface, it is a natural alternative source of gap anisotropy and should be discussed.
concerns.quote: The model omits the CDW... it is a natural alternative source of gap anisotropy and should at least be discussed.

concerns.concern: With V0 < V1 = V2 on a triangular lattice, chiral E-irrep states may be favored. The authors should state whether self-consistent solutions started from generic initial conditions and whether time-reversal-breaking solutions were checked.
concerns.quote: whether time-reversal-breaking or E-irrep solutions were checked and found higher in free energy.

concerns.concern: The model gives a K-pocket gap ratio of about 0.1 with a weak shoulder, while experiment shows a ratio of about 0.6 with a strong feature. The comparison should be presented as qualitative at best.
concerns.quote: The comparison is qualitative at best and should be presented that way.

concerns.concern: Out-of-plane spin polarization at K in surface-sensitive spin-ARPES also appears in centrosymmetric bulk 2H compounds through hidden spin polarization. It should not be listed as evidence of decoupling.
concerns.quote: This evidence should not be listed as confirming decoupling.

concerns.concern: A Tc close to the monolayer value could instead result from charge transfer from SnS. This alternative should be discussed.
concerns.quote: charge transfer from SnS is an obvious alternative cause of the enhancement from 0.8 K. Please discuss it.

concerns.concern: The empirical correlation between multi-gap spectra and weak interlayer coupling rests on a few heterogeneous datasets. The MBE monolayer counterexample is set aside and the 4Hb evidence is indirect. Multi-gap superconductivity should not be called intrinsic to isolated 1H layers.
concerns.quote: The literature correlation is thin.

concerns.concern: The finite DOS at EF on the SnS surface could come from well-documented charge transfer from TaS2. Spatial uniformity does not establish that it is intrinsic to SnS.
concerns.quote: The authors attribute it to the SnS layer itself because it is spatially uniform, but uniformity does not establish that.

concerns.concern: The 4Hb-TaS2 comparison is weak because the 1T layer there is a correlated CDW insulator, whereas the SnS surface has finite DOS at EF.
concerns.quote: The 4Hb comparison is weak, because the 1T layer there is a correlated insulator with a CDW gap

concerns.concern: The Stanescu-Das Sarma argument applies to weak tunnel coupling with Fermi-surface mismatch. That is not obviously the regime of a covalently bonded misfit interface.
concerns.quote: The Stanescu-Das Sarma argument [78] applies to weak tunnel coupling with Fermi-surface mismatch, which is not obviously the regime

concerns.concern: Measurements that would discriminate intrinsic from proximity SnS superconductivity are requested. These are the temperature dependence of the SnS gap versus the 1H gaps, vortex core profiles on both terminations in the same field, and tunneling at SnS step edges or regions with different SnS thickness.
concerns.quote: Discriminating measurements would be: the temperature dependence of the SnS gap compared with the 1H gaps

concerns.concern: The 'internal pressure' explanation for SnS superconductivity, by analogy with high-pressure SnS, is speculative and should be labeled as such or removed.
concerns.quote: The "internal pressure" explanation... is speculative and should be labeled as such or removed.

concerns.concern: An in-plane Hc2 enhancement of only about 2 over the Pauli limit is modest for a true monolayer Ising superconductor. Its implications for the degree of decoupling or the strength of Ising SOC should be discussed.
concerns.quote: an enhancement of about 2 is modest for Ising superconductivity in a "true monolayer" limit

concerns.concern: The kz-independence argument uses an inner potential borrowed from another compound. The c-axis constant used, proof that the photon-energy range spans M and L, and a quantitative bound on kz dispersion are missing.
concerns.quote: give a quantitative bound on any kz dispersion or M-point splitting.

concerns.concern: The Discussion cites strong transport anisotropy, but only Hc2 anisotropy is shown. A rho_c/rho_ab measurement would directly support decoupling.
concerns.quote: The Discussion cites "strong transport anisotropy", but only Hc2 anisotropy is shown.

concerns.concern: The spin-polarization axis is labeled P [%] with range ±0.5, which would be unconvincingly small if literal. The label should be clarified and error bars given.
concerns.quote: If this is literally percent, the polarization is far too small to be convincing.

concerns.concern: The spin-orbit coupling lambda = 0.3 eV exceeds the hopping t = 0.25 eV. This should be justified against the known spin splitting of TaS2.
concerns.quote: lambda = 0.3 eV exceeds t = 0.25 eV. Please justify this against the known spin splitting of TaS2.

concerns.concern: The energy scales of the main-text calculations and the SM calculations differ by about a factor of 5. The Fig. 5 parameters should be given and the discrepancy explained.
concerns.quote: differ by a factor of about 5. Please give the parameters used for Fig. 5

concerns.concern: The text calls triplet/singlet ratios of about 0.27 and 0.08 'comparable', which overstates them.
concerns.quote: The inset of Fig. 5e gives triplet/singlet ratios of about 0.27 and 0.08 at t_perp = 0. The text describes these weights as "comparable".

concerns.concern: The statement that s+f mixing creates a gap imbalance between K and K' is physically wrong by time reversal. What differs is the gap on the two spin-split bands.
concerns.quote: Time reversal relates (K, up) to (K', down), so the gap magnitude of a given band cannot differ between K and K'.

concerns.concern: The pairing interaction is described inconsistently in the text (on-site repulsion, weak repulsion, suppressed attraction), while the SM uses an attractive V0.
concerns.quote: Please describe the interaction consistently.

concerns.concern: Abrupt steps in the low-temperature H || c resistance curves look like flux jumps or contact artifacts. They affect the 50% Hc2 criterion and need explanation.
concerns.quote: These look like flux jumps or contact artifacts, and they directly affect the 50% criterion at low T.

concerns.concern: The quoted Pauli-limit enhancement factor of 1.95 does not match the reviewer's recalculation of about 1.88.
concerns.quote: The Pauli-limit factor is quoted as 1.95... I get about 1.88.

concerns.concern: Because the structure is incommensurate along one axis, the symmetry statements about inversion need to be made more carefully.
concerns.quote: Since the structure is incommensurate along one axis, the symmetry statements also need to be made more carefully.

concerns.concern: A Discussion sentence says the f-wave component becomes comparable in the strongly coupled case, which inverts the main conclusion. It should say weakly coupled or decoupled.
concerns.quote: This should be the weakly coupled, or decoupled, case. The error inverts the main conclusion as written.

concerns.concern: Sample characterization is missing: number of crystals per technique, whether the same batch was used, composition (EDS/WDS), structural confirmation of the misfit periodicity excluding other stacking variants, and the Tc distribution.
concerns.quote: Please give sample information: number of crystals measured by each technique; whether STM, ARPES and transport used the same growth batch

concerns.concern: Bulk evidence for the CDW is needed to explain why there is no resistive anomaly while the STM FFT shows CDW peaks. The incommensurate CDW wavevector also needs comment.
concerns.quote: Bulk evidence for the CDW (XRD superlattice, Raman, or ARPES gap) would clarify why no resistive anomaly is seen

concerns.concern: The STM critical field and coherence length do not quantitatively match the transport Hc2 values as claimed. The different criteria used should be stated.
concerns.quote: Please reconcile, and state that the criteria differ (50% resistive vs disappearance of the STM gap).

concerns.concern: The coherence length is quoted inconsistently (35 ± 5 nm vs 45 ± 10 nm). Extracting it from an exponential fit to the zero-bias DOS is only approximate.
concerns.quote: The coherence length is 35 +/- 5 nm from the vortex in the main text but 45 +/- 10 nm in SM Sec. V.

concerns.concern: The SM resistivity analysis is inconsistent. The residual resistivity conflicts with Fig. 2a, a prefactor's uncertainty exceeds its value, the saturation discussion is unsupported by near-linear data, and the Bloch-Grueneisen integrand has a typo.
concerns.quote: the parallel-resistor discussion of "saturating resistivity" is not supported by Fig. 2a, which is close to linear.

concerns.concern: Tc is quoted inconsistently (3.1, 3.05, 3.14 K). The transition width and criterion should be given.
concerns.quote: Please harmonize, and give the transition width and criterion.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 2a caption gives the temperature range reversed, and the data extend below 1.7 K.
concerns.quote: Fig. 2a caption: "1.7 K >= T >= 300 K" is reversed, and the data extend below 1.7 K.

concerns.concern: Figure cross-references in the Fig. 4 and Fig. 1e captions point to the wrong panels.
concerns.quote: These should be 1d and 1f (topographies). Fig. 1e caption: "same location as (c)" should be (d).

concerns.concern: The text says the first derivative of the spectra is shown while the figure shows d2I/dV2. One convention should be used.
concerns.quote: "we present the first derivative of the spectra" while the figure shows d2I/dV2.

concerns.concern: The model is introduced as a single 2H-TaS2 layer but is then a bilayer model.
concerns.quote: "minimal, single-orbital tight-binding model ... of a single 2H-TaS2 layer" is followed by a bilayer model. Please clarify.

concerns.concern: Footnote [71] about a superposition being an inversion eigenfunction is unclear about which superposition is meant.
concerns.quote: Footnote [71], "The superposition of the two is obviously an eigen-function of inversion", is unclear.

concerns.concern: SM Sec. VII.C.2 calls finite-t_perp cases 'isolated', contains a wording error about the mixing, and labels panels 't' instead of t_perp.
concerns.quote: Figs. 11 and 12 are described as "two isolated H layers" at t_perp = 0.1 and 0.2 eV, which is not isolated.

concerns.concern: The SM has a broken figure cross-reference and multiple typos.
concerns.quote: The SM figure reference "Figs. VII C 1, 8, 9" is a broken cross-reference. There are several typos

concerns.concern: Several references are garbled or contain encoding errors.
concerns.quote: Ref. [34] is garbled, and Refs. [39] and [41] contain encoding errors.
